where: crates/blaze-graph/src/footprint.rs (`Charge::ask_purge`), crates/blaze-cargo/src/serve/plane.rs (`Plane::poll`, the purge it lets go), crates/blaze-cargo/src/serve/daemon.rs (`Still`)
what: A cold `blaze run -p smoke` stalled after 48-52 s with 11 ready nodes and nothing running: `blaze stalled: ... no task ran or was ready` beside nodes listed `Ready`. The lane was briefed that awaited crates (hir-def deps/awaited.rs) held the tasks; the code says they do not: a serve releases the blocked crate of every ready unit, and the 22 tasks never left memory admission (`blaze_graph::Plane::pick`). The client had been told so all along (`build paused: daemon at 187.9 of 191 GiB, waiting on 3 tasks`, last `daemon at 9 of 191 GiB, waiting for the system's memory pressure to pass`) but the admission spans said `a work thread` and the stall said nothing of admission.
cost: two stalled cold builds on the VM, a runner's round of profile queries, and a lane briefed on the wrong mechanism; every project with a build script or proc macro failed its cold build on the head
cause: Read from the code, to be confirmed by the rerun (not measured): the plane asks its driver for a purge and then asked no other until a reading after a purge; the driver (changed 2026-11-12 to not chase a purge nothing waits for) lets a purge go with no purged reading when a task ended in its lag and nothing was held back as it landed; from then on no purge is asked, `Charge::alone_ok` is never true, and a task that starts only alone (a guess over the whole budget: a program never measured) waits for good, holding back every other task with memory once it is the starved one.
whys: Why did the build stall? Ready tasks were never started by memory admission though nothing was granted and 9 of 191 GiB was held.
Why were they not started? A task that fits only alone needs a footprint reading taken after a purge, and none came.
Why did none come? The plane had asked once and waited for the answer for good; the driver had let that purge go unanswered.

Why could the driver do that? The ask was a flag in the plane with no bound and no owner of the answer: the plane's wait was ended only by the driver's side of a protocol stated in a comment, and the driver's rule changed without the plane's.

Why did no test catch it? The footprint simulation's driver always chases a purge (`Sim::land_purge`) and its oracle is safety alone (the ceiling); nothing states that a task which fits the budget starts once nothing is granted.

Why was the lane sent to the wrong mechanism? The stall message said `no task ran or was ready` (it meant: no thread task had ended untaken) and named no rule of admission; the admission span says `memory` only when another task with memory started over the waiter, so a wait for memory in which nothing fit was labelled `a work thread`.
class: a wait whose waker is another component's unstated obligation (A: lost wakeup across a driver/core protocol): the core waits for an answer it asked for once, with no bound, and the driver may drop the question; and its mirror, a stall that names nodes but not the rule holding them
prevention: Done in this lane: `Charge::ask_purge` asks again every PURGE_EVERY_NS while the plane is held back, answered or not, with the invariant stated on it and a test (`a_purge_let_go_unanswered_is_asked_again_so_a_task_alone_starts`); the stall now says how many nodes are ready and unstarted, which are held back for memory, and admission's state (charged, granted, allowance, room, cap, whether a task may start alone and why not, whether a starved task holds the others). Still to do (written in /tmp/awaited-stall/next.md): a liveness oracle in the footprint simulation (a task that fits the budget starts within a bound once nothing is granted) with the driver's let-go modelled and the old rule as its planted bug; the admission span's `memory` label from `waits_for_memory`, not from `passed`; and why 345 first tasks of a cold build are forecast 66 GB each, which runs a 128-thread machine three tasks at a time.
